title: Withdraw a standing founder approval when failure evidence names a run it allowed; report the level each tuple has earned, and grant nothing
problem: An unpaid founder APPROVAL of an exact scope stays in a mission's approved_scopes until a paid run or a restore voids it (greg/missions.py). Nothing else removes it. Reproduced on real booted bodies at #196 head a6c29bbd, with a test founder key, before any change: (1) ineffective run: a standing mission's approved strategy w-bad ran, the check it advances still failed and the engine recorded routing.outcome ineffective; after w-good healed the check and the world drifted, w-bad ran again under its old approval with no new ask (actions w-bad DONE, w-good DONE, w-bad DONE, w-good DONE); (2) refuted closure: approved strategy w ran, the mission held, the separate appraiser re-read a changed world and recorded REFUTED, and at the next cadence w ran again with no ask (w DONE, w DONE). Directive section 59 also asks a question no GREG surface answered: for capability X, action class Y, target Z and budget B, what level of autonomy has evidence earned?
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE, sections 4 (no model or agent manufactures authority), 59 (autonomy is earned per capability, action class, target and budget; no intelligence threshold produces sovereignty), 60 and 67 (kill criteria: second authority plane, autonomous authority escalation, founder burden without gain), the sections the unit spec names
INTENT-2026-09-30-MASTER-BUILD-DIRECTIVE (first issuance of sections 59-64, repeated word for word in the 2026-10-28 reissue)
baseline: a6c29bbd (#196 head when the unit started; #196 is now b1950be2, one test file later): approved_scopes is cleared only by a paid DONE run or by decision.withdrawn {voids_approval: true}, which greg/recovery.py records after a restore. routing.outcome ineffective records and REFUTED appraisals are written but never reach a standing approval. autonomy/levels.py (AutonomyTuple, licence levels) is imported by no GREG Python module. No command reports an earned level per tuple.

alternatives.name: Proposed: a body-tick regression through the existing withdrawal record, plus a read-only earned-level report
alternatives.description: New greg/autonomy.py. failures() names every completed run that failure evidence covers: routing.outcome ineffective for its receipt; for a founder-reconciled run (no receipt), the first measured failing observation of a check it advances, judged by the engine's own blames_strategy; or a REFUTED appraisal of the closure window that holds the run (the window greg/appraisal.py uses). regress() records autonomy.regressed and then decision.withdrawn {voids_approval: true} for each still-standing APPROVAL of that scope asked before the run, the greg/recovery.py pattern the mission fold already reads. One call line in Body.tick runs it before Goal Gravity and the mission engine select. report() and `greg autonomy` fold the ledger per (capability, action class, target pattern, budget band) into SHADOW, RECOMMENDER or SUPERVISED_CANARY, never higher, and write nothing.
advantages: Closes the reproduced defect: after failure evidence the next selection of the scope asks the founder again (20 real-body tests pass; fail-before rows below)
Narrows only: it records withdrawals and never adds to approved_scopes or answers
greg/missions.py, greg/authority.py and greg/appraisal.py untouched; greg/body.py gains one call line and one import name
Answers section 59's question from the ledger alone, with counts, a Wilson bound and what the next level needs
disadvantages: Two more ledger records per regression (autonomy.regressed, decision.withdrawn)
A ledger fold runs every tick while any approval stands
Any REFUTED verdict regresses the approvals of runs in its window, including refutations the action did not cause
Thresholds and tuple boundaries are first choices declared in code, not founder-ratified
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained as the proposal; revisit if founder-device use shows re-asks from refutations the action did not cause are a material share of the founder's asks.

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: the unit spec's one hook inside greg/missions.py's approval fold
alternatives.description: Discard the scope digest from approved_scopes inside the mission fold on mission.compensation_required or on a REFUTED appraisal attributable to the action, and mark the scope's APPROVAL requests consumed, as the paid branch already does.
advantages: One place, no new event type, no extra ledger records
No per-tick fold outside the mission book
disadvantages: greg/missions.py is edited by open PRs #201, #209, #214, #228 and #229, so it waits on five PRs

Its headline trigger is vacuous: mission.compensation_required is recorded only by _compensate for ABANDONED or SUPERSEDED missions, which select nothing more (critique 2 of the unit spec; confirmed by review round 2)
It reads no ineffective evidence and no founder-reconciled run, the two routes this unit's tests and reviews found live
alternatives.revival_evidence: After #201, #209, #214, #228 and #229 land, folding the withdrawal into missions.py could replace the extra records if the integrator wants one place; the real-body tests and 21 mutants carry over as its acceptance.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing design: the whole of WU-09, including a founder-signed AUTONOMY_GRANT
alternatives.description: Part A plus Part B: an AUTONOMY_GRANT founder command (greg/founder.py, one branch in greg/body.py), autonomy/levels.py issuance above A0 bound to a verified founder command id, BOUNDED_AUTONOMY through the grant only, and a manage-by-exception view in greg/mission_control.py.
advantages: Reaches the levels above SUPERVISED_CANARY that section 59 lists
Lets founder intervention decline for granted tuples (one row per exception)
Closes the autonomy/levels.py authorized_by string gap
disadvantages: Creates a second approval path beside AuthorityOffice's exact-scope approvals unless it is designed as one path, which is a kill criterion of section 67 and an authority-granting change
Needs a founder decision before it is built (critique 2 of the unit spec)
Touches greg/founder.py, greg/missions.py, greg/body.py and greg/mission_control.py, the same command surface as WU-06 and WU-12
alternatives.revival_evidence: A founder decision on a single authority path for grants above SUPERVISED_CANARY; this unit's report is its read-only input.

alternatives.name: Staged/reversible experiment: shadow the regression first
alternatives.description: Compute failures() every tick and record what would be withdrawn, without withdrawing, until founder-device use measures how many re-asks the rule would cause.
advantages: Measures founder burden before changing behaviour
Zero behaviour change on the body
disadvantages: Leaves the reproduced defect live: a scope proven ineffective or refuted keeps running unasked during the shadow period
There is no founder-device use yet to measure (VEPMC 0), so the shadow period has no end condition today
alternatives.revival_evidence: If the founder finds the re-asks a burden, a shadow mode for the non-attributable refutation case only could be added behind a founder-signed setting.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: A founder approval given once for an unpaid exact scope keeps authorizing that scope after its run was shown ineffective or its closure was refuted, so GREG re-runs a failing action without asking. No surface answers section 59.
advantages: No change to the body tick or the ledger
disadvantages: The reproduced defect stays live on the canonical mission path
Wider worker or node autonomy (WU-03, WU-06) would build on approvals that outlive failure
Section 59's question stays unanswerable from the ledger

roles.position: Section 4 says no model may decide it deserves more privileges, and section 59 says autonomy is earned per tuple. An approval that outlives evidence of failure is privilege kept without evidence. This unit removes that and answers section 59 read-only, without creating any level above SUPERVISED_CANARY. It narrows only.
material_concerns: Part B (AUTONOMY_GRANT, levels.py binding, manage-by-exception view) is not built; spec acceptance tests 4, 5 and 7 are unmet and stay NEEDS_FOUNDER_DECISION
The underlying effect the founder wants (intervention declining without sovereignty) is not shown: in the short run the change adds re-asks, and nothing ran on a founder device
Tuple boundaries and thresholds are the implementer's first choices, not the founder's

roles.position: Existing mechanisms only: the decision.withdrawn voids_approval record greg/recovery.py already writes, the mission fold that already reads it, the engine's routing.outcome and blames_strategy, and the appraiser's own closure windows. dissent.handling: Recorded with thresholds; neither entry blocks a draft. The first blocks nothing unless its threshold is met; the second is a founder policy choice.

entries.position: Regress only on a refutation attributable to the run's action, as the unit spec worded it, and not on every REFUTED verdict in the window; a reconciled run that worked should not lose its approval merely because it has no Gate receipt.
entries.rationale: Every non-attributable re-ask is founder burden without gain (section 67), and the 'Jarvis' effect is declining intervention.
entries.evidence_threshold: Founder-device evidence that re-asks from refutations the action did not cause are a material share of the founder's asks, or the founder says so
entries.review_trigger: First founder-device use, or the appraiser gaining cause attribution

entries.position: An open compensation of an external or irreversible effect should hold a tuple's level down, not only be counted.
entries.rationale: A tuple could read SUPERVISED_CANARY while one of its effects still awaits undoing.
entries.evidence_threshold: A founder ruling, or a ledger where a tuple reaches SUPERVISED_CANARY with an external or irreversible compensation open
entries.review_trigger: The Part B decision, or the first such ledger
